text: Doraemon, the co-protagonist of the anime and manga series, is a cat-like robot from the future with yellow skin who originally had ears, but they were eaten by a robotic mouse, causing him to become blue-skinned and heartbroken. People often mistake him for a raccoon dog, which frustrates him. He is sent back in time by Sewashi Nobi, Nobita's great-great-grandson, to assist Nobita. Doraemon possesses a 4-dimensional pocket from which he retrieves futuristic tools, gadgets, and playthings from a future department store. He tends to panic during emergencies, frantically pulling out a needed item only to produce a large number of unrelated household items. Despite his frequent mishaps, Doraemon is friendly and intelligent but suffers greatly due to Nobita's behavior. Since his arrival, he has lived as the unofficial fourth member of Nobita's family, acting like a second son to Nobita's parents, as he needs to eat and sleep. He is deeply afraid of mice, a fear stemming from the robot mouse that ate his ears, and often reacts with devastating gadgets when confronted with them; Nobita usually saves him in such situations. Although he lacks fingers in most media (though sometimes has bumps resembling fingers in his hands), he can hold objects due to suction cups in his hands. His favorite food is Dorayaki or Doracake. He has been shown to date a normal female cat named Mi Chan. He is the elder brother of Dorami, another robot from the future, who is at least as smart as Doraemon. Nobita Nobi, the other co-protagonist, wears glasses, a red or yellow polo shirt with a white collar, and blue or black shorts with white socks and light blue shoes. He is not good at sports but is skilled at shooting and string figures. He is the son of Tamako and Nobisuke Nobi, the future father of Nobisuke (his son), and the future husband or boyfriend of Shizuka and great-great-grandfather of Sewashi. Shizuka Minamoto, nicknamed Shizuka-chan, is a smart, kind, and pretty girl often associated with the color pink, wearing a pink shirt and skirt. The name "Shizuka" means "Quiet." She is Nobita's best friend and love-interest and does not avoid him due to his poor grades or laziness; instead, she encourages him, though she usually fails. She bathes several times a day, but is frequently interrupted by Nobita, Gian, or Suneo, often due to misuse of Doraemon's gadgets like the Anywhere Door. Her skirt is often flipped by Nobita's gadget misuse or the wind. Scenes showing her bathing or underwear have been removed from dubbed versions in India, Europe, the U.S., and the U.K. Her true passions are sweet potatoes and the violin, both of which she plays poorly, and she reluctantly takes piano lessons due to her mother's wishes. She is an animal lover and keeps two pets: a dog saved from illness by Nobita and Doraemon, and a canary that runs away repeatedly, leading Nobita and Shizuka to chase it. She sometimes likes handsome TV idols and is close to her classmate Dekisugi, though they remain friends. Takeshi Goda, known as Gian, is a strong, quick-tempered bully who frequently steals others' belongings, especially Nobita's and Suneo's, under the excuse of "borrowing" them unless the item is damaged. He has a terrible singing voice, which causes nausea in listeners; even when Nobita and Doraemon try to mute it in a silent world, the lyrics written on a board have the same effect. Despite his poor singing, a girl once liked it, and in some films, his singing is enhanced into a weapon. When he hears a recording of himself, he denies it is his voice and threatens to beat the person who sang it poorly. Gian is confident in cooking, but his homemade food is often terrible. Though he is seen as intimidating, he is sensitive and cries easily when touched, values his friends deeply, and has a soft spot for his younger sister Jaiko, often trying to prevent her from getting into trouble. He is fearful of his mother, who frequently punishes him. His catchphrase is "What's mine is mine. What's yours is also mine," known as Gianism in Japan. Suneo Honekawa, known as Sneech in the English dub, is a fox-faced, rich, and spoiled child who loves to show off his wealth, especially to Nobita, often provoking envy. He frequently teases Nobita and pushes him aside when inviting Gian and Shizuka to his parties. Despite his boastful nature, he is one of Nobita's closest friends and often asks for help from Nobita and Doraemon. In films, he is reluctant to join adventures and avoids trouble, showing cowardice. He has extensive scientific knowledge, is a talented artist and designer, and is extremely cunning. He is self-conscious about his height, being the shortest in class, and often brags about himself, sometimes staring in the mirror. He likes steak and melon and tries to win Shizuka's favor. Dorami is Doraemon's younger sister, yellow-skinned with a large red bow replacing her ears and a flower tail replacing her kitsune tails. She shares half the oil from a can with Doraemon during her creation, making them siblings. She lives in 22nd-century Tokyo with Sewashi and visits Nobita using the time machine when Doraemon is off-duty or during his health checkup. She likes melonpan and is afraid of cockroaches like Nobita's mother. She is a more advanced robot than Doraemon, capable of producing 10,000 horsepower compared to Doraemon's 129.3, and is the smartest student in her school, with better gadget skills. In one story, Nobita tries to replace Doraemon with her due to her superior abilities, but quickly realizes she does not understand him and does not tolerate his antics. She has her own spin-off manga, and in The Doraemons series, she is the love interest of Dora-the-Kid, Doraemon's friendly rival. Nobita's paternal grandmother, also known as Grandma, died when Nobita was in kindergarten before the main storyline. She is kind and eccentric, unlike her husband, and never scolded Nobisuke for not engaging in masculine activities. Nobita remembers her fondly, with many of his positive childhood memories involving her; many of his toys, including his old kendama, were given to him by her. When Nobita travels to the past, she recognizes him as her grandson. She appears in a few episodes and takes care of Nobita in his early years; in one Doraemons manga, she is proud to see him grow into a teenager. Shizuka's cousin appears in a few episodes. A character who lives with Sunetsugu in New York and raised him as his own son, is single, and sometimes appears in Doraemon episodes. He blamed himself for Doraemon being outdated but, after seeing the friendship and brotherhood between Doraemon and Nobita, he abandoned his reset in one episode. A character often seen with Gian and Suneo playing in a vacant lot or baseball field, wearing a baseball cap and often appearing with Haruo. Another character often seen with Gian and Suneo in the same settings, moderately fat, and often appears with Yasuo.
